chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usmaan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

In Paradise is a river, its banks are lined with thriving Houries. So if the Believer passes by one of them and she pleases him, he uproots her, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, plants another in her place.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the river and its banks in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the boundless nature of divine bounty in Jannah, where the 'Houries' are described as 'growing' or 'sprouting' (hanibat), suggesting a living, renewable quality rather than static creation. This imagery underscores the Shia theological emphasis on Allah’s infinite capacity to provide without depletion, reinforcing the believer’s hope in eternal, fresh pleasures.

en.hubeali: H 14747 – And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al-Husayn Bin Usmaan, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws having said:

‘In the Paradise is a river on banks of which are Houries are thriving. So if the Believer passes by one of them, and she pleases him, he uproots her (takes her away). So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Implants another one in her place’.
en.sarwar: 299. And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al-Husayn Bin Usmaan, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said:
